analysis: Examined four changed files. ClusterRuntimeFactsCommand.swift (head 16-77): hidden runtime-facts CLI gains --list-release-models (prints static ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.releaseModels as JSON), --release-candidates (computes release facts from a local folder, round-trips canonical bytes through the strict decoder at head 56-57) and stderr notes for unqualified declared families. validate() (head 29-39) enforces mutually exclusive option sets. It is local, operator-run metadata tooling with no network, secret or serving authority; the facts' trust comes from coordinator registration and qualification (A-017, T-054), which is platform-owned and outside this evidence. The integration pass should confirm that the coordinator, not this self-reported CLI output, authoritatively qualifies cluster builds and models. A provider (ADV-001) can already run arbitrary code locally, so no new boundary was found. ClusterSetupWizardCommand.swift head 106 plumbs request.scope into service.wizard.servingScope. The effect depends on unseen ClusterService/ClusterOnboardingRequest code, for example whether local-only scope can be widened to public serving. The serving decision still depends on coordinator authorization (TB-011/A-016), so this is a question for integration, not a finding. Test fixture MemberFixtureServicePart.swift head 28-31 writes the health-file env value to a test directory; it is test-only. PlacementSetupCheck.swift head 1260-1264 updates the test for the new publicModels parameter of publicTrafficLine. With an empty declaration, the test expects an unqualified family to remain not qualified. Integration should check that the non-test publicTrafficLine/ClusterPublicModels logic cannot mark a declared family qualified without a parity record. Source is not in this batch. No concrete regression was identified.
